chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him, 'If a man is appointed guardian over an orphan's wealth, can he borrow from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to borrow from the wealth of an orphan who was in his care.'
ai.seo_question: Can a guardian borrow money from an orphan's estate?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of a guardian borrowing from an orphan's wealth, citing the practice of Ali ibn Al-Husayn (AS) as a precedent. It addresses the legal ruling regarding the management and usage of orphan's assets by their appointed guardians. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often interpreted as allowing the guardian to use the funds for the orphan's benefit or for necessary expenses, provided the amount is repaid, reflecting the practical flexibility in managing waqf-like assets under guardianship.
